headline: Benchmarks test ML models for single-cell perturbation and cancer prediction
label: Benchmarking Machine Learning In Biology
summary: Foundation-model embeddings and diffusion models now face standardized evaluation for perturbation response and cancer tasks, with calibration and leakage…
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation design for machine learning in biology rather than new architectures. PertDiffBench standardizes comparison of diffusion models for transcriptomic perturbation response across single-cell and bulk RNA-seq, while ReconEval benchmarks gene expression reconstruction from single-cell latent spaces spanning PCA, autoencoders, VAEs and foundation model embeddings. A cancer-focused preprint evaluates foundation-model image and transcriptomic embeddings, testing image-omics fusion and conformal prediction, with calibrated uncertainty treated as a primary output. Other items are task-specific frameworks rather than benchmarks: PertCurve models perturbation response trajectories in Perturb-seq data, DISCERN infers single-cell drug sensitivity from cell-type-specific networks, and scMagnifier resolves cell subtypes through consensus clustering. What is new across this set is attention to benchmark construction and calibrated uncertainty as outputs, not accuracy alone.
